@@ -739,6 +739,21 @@ everything target-specific is independent.
 | D40 | GLR + ALL(\*) coexist      | **Both retained, not merged. LR(1)/LALR/IELR is the self-hosted core. `Gramaire.Glr` is the generalized recognizer + diagnostics engine: `forest` enumerates all parses (proving ambiguity) and `explainP` powers `explain-conflict` (LALR-artifact vs resolved vs genuine). `Gramaire.Ll` is the ALL(\*) `ll-star` strategy: top-down ATN-driven prediction that commits to one alternative, and the shared ATN substrate for ANTLR (and future Bison) interop.**                                                                                                                                  | Answers "drop GLR for ALL(\*)?": no — they solve different problems. ALL(\*) *resolves* ambiguity (picks one alternative by prediction, like ANTLR); GLR *enumerates* it (the forest), which is what proves a grammar ambiguous and what the conflict differential needs. Replacing GLR with ALL(\*) would silently drop ambiguity reporting and gut `explain-conflict`, while ALL(\*) still earns its keep as the opt-in top-down strategy and the ATN foundation the foreign-format converters share. The one lateral move considered — shrinking GLR to an Earley diagnostic recognizer — is deferred, not a replacement.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
 | D41 | Context-sensitivity        | **Post-parse CST fold is canonical for symbol-table/declared-before-use checks (extends D7/D24/D25's action-as-catamorphism model); ANTLR-style semantic predicates, if built, are scoped exclusively to the `ll-star` ATN strategy (never Core/LR, never the scanner) and gated on an IR-level effect declaration so they survive backend export; the Bison/Yacc "lexer hack" (parser-fed scanner state) is rejected outright.**                                                                                                                                                                 | The verified LR(1)/LALR/IELR core and the self-host lexer oracle (`Test.LexerSelfHost`) depend on tokenization being parse-independent — a parser-driven scanner would invalidate that guarantee for a narrow C-typedef-style win that `%external` (D33) already covers for genuinely non-regular lexis. A pure fold over the finished CST reuses the existing action/Visitor machinery (D24/D25) with zero engine risk and no interaction with incremental reparse (D18/D22), so it is the default answer. Predicates are real (ANTLR's mechanism, and the ATN substrate already exists per D40) but only make sense where prediction happens — top-down ALL(\*) — and must declare their symbol-table effects in the IR before Phase 3's `.g4` import work relies on them, or ANTLR-imported predicates silently vanish on re-export.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
 | D42 | IR predicate effect        | **`rules[].predicate: { reads: string[], writes: string[] }` — optional, additive (irVersion stays 0). Presence flags the rule's action an ALL(\*) semantic predicate (D-predicates) rather than a value-building one; the declared keys are author-chosen and opaque to the core (no built-in symbol-table mechanism exists) — they exist purely so a consumer can reason about or invalidate a predicate without evaluating its opaque body. Ships as inert plumbing: no front-end producer populates it yet (`{%? %}` stays unparsed), built ahead of that wiring, same as `atn`/`glr` were.** | Unblocks two dependents stuck waiting on "design it first": the ANTLR importer's predicate carry-through (`all-star-port-plan.md` Phase 3 — the field existing doesn't mean the importer populates it yet, that wiring is still separate) and `incremental-spec.md`'s R22/R23 predicate-invalidation rules, which need `reads`/`writes` to reference as something concrete rather than a promise. Mirrors the additive-optional-field pattern already used for `extras`/`recovery`/`glr`/`atn`/`lexer` (`IR.scala`, `IRDecode.scala`, `IRValidate.scala`, `ir-schema.json`) exactly — encode omits the key when absent, decode/validate are presence-guarded, and the committed goldens (`test/golden/*.ir.json`) stay byte-unchanged (`IRGoldenSuite`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
+| D43 | Platform positioning + editor/IDE tooling | **Gramaire is positioned as a converter-hub-first, standard-track EBNF format (earn "the standard" via a second real round-trip, not by declaring it) and as a learning/debugging/analysis platform. "One portable Scala drives CLI/Web/JVM/WASM; TypeScript is web-glue only" is codified as a standing architectural rule, not a new direction — the Lab already calls Scala.js-compiled `core`/`lab` from `worker.ts` rather than reimplementing engine logic in TS. Roadmap additions, in dependency order: (1) finish D38 (Bison/yacc import+export) bundled with D39 (comment round-trip) as one unit, tested as `import(export(x))` fidelity, not just "parses"; (2) Tier-1 LSP server (JVM, native-image, reuses the existing `cli` packaging) gated on Phase F's incremental core (D18/D22) — this is the hinge every client below depends on; (3) VSCode extension as a thin TS activation shell speaking LSP-over-stdio to the same native-image binary, no engine logic in TS; (4) JetBrains plugin embedding the JVM core jar directly (no protocol layer needed — cheaper architecturally, but scored down on effort for platform/maintenance unknowns since the team has no prior JetBrains-plugin experience), sequenced *after* VSCode so the LSP contract is proven first; (5) standalone app as a packaging exercise over the same native-image binary + the Lab's static frontend, last since it is the cheapest once the LSP server exists; (6) MCP server deferred, not rejected — the CLI's JSON output (`emit --backend ir`) already covers stateless agent use, so MCP only earns its keep once Phase F's incremental server holds parse state worth keeping warm across calls.** | Debated internally (2026-07-04): the "standard" framing was contested until tied to a testable round-trip-fidelity bar rather than a positioning claim; LSP-before-editor-clients was contested until framed as risk sequencing (prove the server contract once via the cheapest client before a second, harder-to-iterate-on client depends on it); JetBrains-is-cheap was contested (classloader/plugin-API-skew/no prior experience are real, uncounted costs) and the roadmap value/effort scores below reflect that pushback; MCP was contested on "name the concrete benefit or cut it" grounds and tied explicitly to D22's incremental-as-capability gate rather than treated as a free add-on. New precondition surfaced by the debate: the D29 document-structure contract must be frozen before any editor extension ships syntax/folding logic against it, since a shipped extension hard-codes that contract in a way an IR version bump does not. |
